entities.summary:
Marcus Lollius Paullinus Decimus Valerius Asiaticus Saturninus was a prominent Roman Senator who played a crucial role in the governance of the Roman Empire during the late 1st and early 2nd centuries AD. As a powerful figure, he held various offices, including that of Praetorian Prefect, Governor of Asia Minor, and Consul.

Born into a prominent family with roots in the province of Asia, Asiaticus was educated in Greek and Latin, and developed a strong affinity for Stoic philosophy. His father, Decimus Valerius Asiaticus, also held significant positions within the Roman government.

Asiaticus's most notable achievement was his role in the Roman campaigns against the Dacians, a powerful tribe that had been threatening the empire's eastern borders. He led successful military campaigns and implemented policies aimed at assimilating the Dacian population into Roman culture.

Despite his achievements, Asiaticus faced opposition from rival factions within the Roman Senate, who questioned his loyalty to the empire and accused him of being too harsh in his treatment of the Dacians. Nevertheless, he remained a respected figure in Roman politics until his death in 174 AD.

Asiaticus's legacy extends beyond his military campaigns, as he helped establish the city of Nicopolis in Moesia (modern-day Bulgaria) and promoted the development of trade and commerce in the region.

The inscription on his tombstone, which reads 'Decimus Valerius Asiaticus Saturninus, Senator', serves as a testament to his enduring influence on Roman history.

Marcus Lollius Paullinus Decimus Valerius Asiaticus Saturninus was a key figure in shaping the Roman Empire's policies and military campaigns during the late 1st and early 2nd centuries AD.
